full_judgment:
2. In respect of Greater Dhaka City Flood protection Embankment the respondent was given by the petitioner a work order foot Taka 1,75,00,00.00. Dispute arose between the parties about enhancement of rates for payment of bills and by mutual agreement Mr. Justice Maksum-ul-Hakim was appointed the Sole Arbitrator. The proceedings could not be completed on several extensions of time for various reasons. The respondent then filed Miscellaneous (Arbitration) Case No. 79 of 1994 under section 11 of the Arbitration Act before the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for appointment of a new Arbitrator in place of the above-named Sole Arbitrator. The petitioner filed objection but the said sole Arbitrator expressed his desire to be relieved of his responsibility. By an order dated 20-8-94 the learned Subordinate Judge relieved Mr. Justice Maksum-ul-Hakim of his responsibilities as Arbitrator and directed the parties to suggest two names each for appointment as Arbitration. The petitioner suggested names of two Engineers and the respondent suggested the names of Mr. Justice KM Subhan and Mr. Maksudur Rahman. citing the latter as a Justice. On 4-8-94 the learned Subordinate Judge appointed Mr. Moksudur Rahman as the Sole Arbitrator taking the view that by a Memo dated 15-4-89 the petitioner passed an office order directing that in respect of claims exceeding Taka 50 Lacs a Justice should be appointed as an Arbitrator. On 15-9-94 the petitioner by filing an application objected in the appointment of Mr. Moksudur Rahman as an Arbitrator. On 15-9-94 the petitioner by filing an application objected to the appointment of Mr. Moksudur Rahman as an Arbitrator contending that he resigned as a Judge before his confirmation and being a practicing lawyer since then he was not a proper person for appointment as an Arbitrator and that the said appointment was erroneous. The petitioner prayed for appointment of an Engineer from its own list submitted earlier as also a retired Judge of the Supreme Court as arbitrators in the case. The learned Subordinate Judge did not pass any order on the petitioner's application dated 15-9-94. The petitioner filed another application on 18-9-94 reiterating the above prayer and a further application for stay of the arbitration proceedings till the application dated 15-9-94 was disposed of Mr. Moksudur Rahman continued with the arbitration proceedings to a great hurry and the petitioner's lawyers participated in the arbitration proceedings on protest. As Mr. Moksudur Rahman was conducting the proceedings in a hurry the petitioner's lawyers were compelled to withdraw from the arbitration proceedings on 24-10-94 and filed an application before the Subordinate Judge on 25-10-94 alleging that the petitioner apprehends that they will not get proper justice from him. By an order dated 6-11-94 the learned Subordinate Judge directed the parties to pay equally the fees of the Arbitrator amounting to Taka 40,000.00. Thereafter the petitioner filed a revisional application Civil Order No. 4091 of 1994 against the orders of the Subordinate Judge dated 26-10-94 (holding that the conduct of the arbitration did not show anything that the party would not get Justice from him) and 6-11-94 and the High Court Division, without issuing any Rule, directed the Subordinate Judge to dispose of the applications filed by petitioner on 15-9-94 and 18-9-94 by 8-1-95. The Subordinate judge thereafter heard and disposed of the said two applications and by an order dated 21-1-95 held that there was no law that if a Judge was not confirmed he could not be appointed as an Arbitrator. The Arbitrator has already filed his award and if the petitioner is aggrieved by the same it can challenge the award as it thinks necessary. 

 6. The Arbitrator has filed the award and if it is the case of the petitioner that the Arbitrator has misconducted himself in the proceedings the petitioner is free to agitate the same in a proper forum.
